# AGENTS.md — AI Tool Usage Guide

Tool-neutral guidance for AI coding tools (Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) working in this repository. Generated by `onecxt adapt` from the canonical project overview and `.onecxt/RULES.md` — do not edit by hand. Skills are auto-discovered per-tool from their respective stub directories (`.claude/skills/`, `.opencode/skills/`, `.cursor/rules/skill-*.mdc`, …); no routing table is inlined here.

## What this project is

one-context is a workspace control plane that keeps many repositories, many
agents, and many AI coding tools aligned on one shared context. Canonical
intent is written once — in `meta/*.yaml`, `.onecxt/RULES.md`,
`knowledge/`, and `skills/` — and then generated into each tool's native
format by `onecxt adapt`.

## Core building blocks

- **meta/ manifests** — declarative registries: repositories
  (`meta/repos.yaml`), workspaces (`meta/workspaces.yaml`), agents
  (`meta/agents.yaml`), and shared behavior profiles
  (`meta/profiles.yaml`).
- **.onecxt/RULES.md** — the single constraint surface, inlined verbatim
  into every adapter's startup context.
- **knowledge/** — canonical notes and conventions. Files or directories
  referenced from manifests are expanded into exports; files carrying
  `visibility: private` frontmatter are excluded from collection.
- **skills/** — reusable agent skills. Each skill is one directory with a
  `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter + instructions); adapters publish them to
  each tool's native skill surface.
- **features/** — spec-driven change flow (spec → tech design → test
  report → delivery note) with an index enforced by `onecxt doctor`.
- **Adapters** — per-tool generators included in `onecxt adapt`:
  `claude_code`, `codex`, `cursor` (opt-in via `--only cursor`), `hermes`,
  `openclaw`, `opencode`, `pi`. Cursor is skipped by default because its
  always-on rules would inflate every chat.

## How it behaves

- `onecxt doctor` cross-checks manifests, knowledge references, feature
  index closure, and rules presence; it is warnings/errors only — it never
  mutates files.
- `onecxt adapt <workspace>` regenerates generated surfaces and refuses to
  overwrite files that no longer carry the generated marker (protecting
  hand edits); `adapt --check` verifies the tree is in sync.
- `onecxt context export <workspace>` emits a tool-neutral bundle (JSON or
  Markdown) of repos, profiles, and knowledge for any consumer.

## Project Rules — one-context workspace

These rules are the canonical constraint surface for every AI coding tool in
this workspace. They are inlined verbatim into each tool's startup context by
`onecxt adapt` — the generated copies are read-only mirrors of this file.

## Canonical sources

- Single source of truth (SoT) lives in tracked, hand-written files:
  `meta/*.yaml` (repos, workspaces, agents, profiles), `.onecxt/RULES.md`,
  `knowledge/01_Compiled/**`, and `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- Files carrying the generated marker (`GENERATED by onecxt adapt` …) are
  build outputs. Never hand-edit them; change the SoT and rerun
  `onecxt adapt` instead.
- `AGENTS.md` at the repository root is generated the same way. Regenerate it
  after changing the project overview or this rules file.

## Workflow

- Validate manifests before and after manifest or knowledge edits:
  `onecxt doctor`. Errors must be fixed; warnings should be acknowledged.
- Feature work flows through `features/`: spec → tech design → implement →
  test report → delivery note. Use `features/_template/` as the starting
  point and keep `features/INDEX.md` in sync (doctor enforces the index).
- Changes stay repository-scoped. Before touching shared files, confirm the
  change belongs to the current feature or is an explicit maintenance task.

## Safety and scope

- Never add secrets, credentials, tokens, or private keys to the workspace.
  Per-machine settings belong in git-ignored `.onecxt/local.yaml` or `.env`
  files, never in tracked manifests.
- Do not invent provider-specific endpoints, proxy routes, or account-level
  configuration in shared files. Such settings are machine-local by contract.
- Destructive operations (deleting branches, force pushes, `--force`
  regenerations) require explicit human approval.
- Keep framework implementation under `packages/one-context/`; business code
  belongs in repositories registered in `meta/repos.yaml`.
- Keep generated paths inside the workspace root.

## Knowledge hygiene

- Knowledge notes marked private via frontmatter (`visibility: private`) are
  excluded from context exports and knowledge-graph scans. Respect that
  boundary when summarizing or linking.
- Cross-file references use root-relative `@path/to/file.md` syntax inside
  `knowledge/`, `docs/`, and `features/`; dangling references fail doctor
  checks.

## Communication style

- Report work in plain language: what changed, what was verified, what is
  left. Prefer short structured summaries over long prose.
